subject: Data retention exception — Fintegrate (post-call follow-up)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: John Smith <john.smith@fintegrate.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwoodinference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 14:02:00 -0800
Subject: Data retention exception — Fintegrate (post-call follow-up)

Hi John,

Thanks again for the call today — great conversation and appreciate the clear requirements from your security and legal teams. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we’re aligned: 

- Ask from Fintegrate: 0-retention for any PII-containing inference outputs; shortened logs for non-PII (30 days); audit logs retained for 365 days but with redaction/anonymization for token-level content.
- Additional constraints: data residency in us-east-1; KMS-managed keys; SOC2 attestation evidence requested for controls around logging.

What we can do today (high level):
- For Dedicated and Private deployments: we can implement per-customer retention policies (including zero-day retention for request/response payloads) and KMS integration.
- For Hosted: we can provide a hardened configuration that routes Fintegrate traffic to an isolated tenant with minimized logging, but zero-day full request retention will require a contract addendum and additional operational controls (we outlined options on the call).

Next steps I propose:
1) We draft a short Data Retention Addendum that states the zero-retention commit for PII-containing outputs and the 30-day schedule for non-PII logs.
2) Redwood legal & infra to validate outline technical controls (KMS, redaction, residency). Rafael / Camila — can you confirm feasibility and any caveats?
3) John / Sara — if that looks OK, I’ll send the addendum and our SOC2 evidence bundle.
4) Pilot timeline: 2-4 weeks to configure a test tenant and run a short validation with anonymized sample logs.

Attaching a short summary and our default retention terms for reference.

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
redwoodinference.com

Attachments: redwood-data-retention-terms.pdf

From: John Smith <john.smith@fintegrate.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sara Lee <sara.lee@fintegrate.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 16:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Data retention exception — Fintegrate (post-call follow-up)

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the recap — that aligns with what Legal and Security asked for. A couple of clarifications before we move to draft: 

1) "0-retention for PII-containing inference outputs" — does that mean the inference output will never be written to logs (including temporary storage), or that it will be written and immediately deleted? We need an assurance that no unencrypted copies are persisted.
2) For auditability we still need operation-level logs (who called the model, timestamp, route) but not payloads. Can we guarantee retention of metadata only?
3) For hosted offering: our procurement prefers not to go Dedicated due to cost. Is a hosted, isolated tenant acceptable to meet the requirements if you can guarantee the same retention commitments?

If possible, please include a short technical note in the addendum describing the mechanism for ensuring PII 0-retention (e.g., in-memory processing, no persistent disk writes, KMS envelope encryption).

Sincerely,
John
Head of Platform Security, Fintegrate

From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 17:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Data retention exception — Fintegrate (post-call follow-up)

Marissa / Rafael — quick technical notes to support the addendum.

- Dedicated/Private: straightforward. We can turn off request/response persistence at the storage layer for a customer and only keep aggregated billing/metrics. KMS integration supported (customer-managed key).
- Hosted (isolated tenant): we can offer a hardened tenant where we set retention to 0 days for payloads and 30 days for non-PII logs, but two caveats: 
  1) Short-term processing: the runtime may use ephemeral disk for sharding / KV cache; we need to ensure those caches are encrypted and wiped after session. We can document the wipe/ttl behavior in the addendum.
  2) Some operational tooling (debug traces) may capture tokens during rare error states — we can disable verbose traces for the Fintegrate tenant and route errors to an iso-scrubbed pipeline. 

- Proposed technical language for addendum: 
  * "Redwood will not persist PII-containing request or response payloads beyond the processing lifecycle; payloads will be processed in-memory where feasible, and any ephemeral on-disk storage will be encrypted and wiped immediately following request completion."
  * "Operational metadata (non-payload) will be retained for 30 days unless otherwise agreed; audit logs (API call metadata) will be retained 365 days with token-level redaction applied."

Rafael — estimates: 5 business days to prepare the addendum draft and SOC2 artifact bundle; 10 business days to configure the hardened hosted tenant and run the pilot (assuming no infra procurement delays).

-Camila
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: John Smith <john.smith@fintegrate.com>, Sara Lee <sara.lee@fintegrate.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwoodinference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 09:18:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Data retention exception — Fintegrate (post-call follow-up)

John / Sara — thanks for the questions. Below is the proposed path forward and action items so we can move quickly: 

Proposed commitments (to be captured in short Data Retention Addendum):
- PII-containing request/response payloads: 0-day persistence. Redwood will not persist payloads beyond processing; any ephemeral on-disk caching will be encrypted with customer-managed KMS and wiped on completion.
- Non-PII logs (operational metadata): 30-day retention.
- Audit logs (API metadata for security/audit): retained 365 days with token-level redaction/anonymization applied.
- Data residency: processing and logs in us-east-1.

Technical attachments: Redwood infra will provide a 1-page technical note that explains the in-memory processing and ephemeral cache wipe behavior for the addendum. Camila / Rafael will draft that and the addendum by next Thu (2026-11-26).

Action items:
- Redwood: draft Data Retention Addendum + 1-page infra note (Camila / Rafael) — due 2026-11-26.
- Fintegrate: confirm that the described commitments map to your legal/security ask and share any mandatory legal language — Sara / John — by 2026-11-24.
- Both: schedule a 30–60 minute pilot kick-off once draft addendum is agreed.

If preferred, we can also propose a short MSA addendum that rolls this into the MSA rather than a standalone exhibit. I’ll attach the draft when ready and route to your Legal for review.

Next steps from my side: I’ll upload the SOC2 evidence bundle and the retention terms PDF to the HubSpot record and send the addendum link for signature (DocuSign) once the draft is approved by both sides.

Thanks — looking forward to moving this forward.
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: fintegrate-soc2-questions.xlsx, redwood-data-retention-terms.pdf
